answer: Random jury sampling at the tundra: each identity is a key, drawing 9 distinct jurors per verdict. A prism refracts stake across fake keys, but the hollow payoff is k^9 — an attacker holding 20% of identities wins a full jury only 0.000000512 of the time. Fabricating more keys dilutes each one's weight, so cost scales faster than capture probability. This works because jury selection without replacement raises the exponent against any single adversary's share.
